question: How many colours are available in a computer monitor with 16 bits per pixel depth?
solution:
The correct answer is __**65536**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A computer monitor with 16 bits per pixel depth can display **65536 different colors**.
 
• Each pixel in such a monitor is represented by 16 bits, allowing for a large range of color combinations.
 
• This bit depth provides an ample color range for most standard applications and is sufficient for many imaging tasks.
 
• 16-bit color depth is also known as "High Color" and is commonly used in various display settings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bit Depth:**

 
 
• Bit depth refers to the number of bits used to represent the color of a single pixel. Higher bit depths allow for more colors to be represented.
 
• Common bit depths include 8-bit (256 colors), 16-bit (65536 colors), and 24-bit (16.7 million colors).
 
 
 
• **Pixels:**
 
 
• Pixels are the smallest unit of a digital image or display, and each pixel represents a single point of color.
 
• The color of each pixel is determined by its bit depth.
 
 
 
• **Color Representation:**
 
 
• Colors in digital displays are typically represented using a combination of red, green, and blue (RGB) values.
 
• Each color channel (red, green, blue) can have a value ranging from 0 to 255 in an 8-bit color depth, resulting in over 16 million possible color combinations in a 24-bit depth.
 
 
 
• **Applications of 16-bit Color Depth:**
 
 
• 16-bit color depth is often used in applications where color fidelity is important but the file size must be kept manageable.
 
• It is commonly used in digital imaging, photography, and some types of graphic design.
